extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions), Title IX coordinators, and institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX recordkeeping and response obligations
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards governing how recipients must document, retain, disclose, and act on information about sex discrimination under the Department's final Title IX regulations, including recordkeeping, training materials, notification duties, and Coordinator responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain records documenting grievance procedures and outcomes for each complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final regulations, a recipient is required to maintain records documenting the grievance procedures under §106.45, and if applicable §106.46, for each complaint of sex discrimination. This includes records of complaints in which the respondent is found responsible for sexual assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must document dismissals, informal resolution processes that conclude without a finding, and judicial determinations that change the recipient's determination; such records are necessary to demonstrate compliance with Title IX and are required under §106.8(f)(1). The Department will not require deletion of such records when complaints are dismissed or informal resolutions conclude without a finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document notifications to Title IX Coordinator and actions taken (§106.8(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each notification the Title IX Coordinator receives about conduct that may reasonably constitute sex discrimination (including notifications under §106.44(c)(1) or (2)), a recipient must maintain records documenting the actions it took to meet its obligations in §106.44, including its prompt and effective response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.8(f)(2) to refer to “notification the Title IX Coordinator receives of information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination,” aligning recordkeeping to notifications rather than an undefined incident; documentation should show steps taken to investigate, offer supportive measures, and otherwise comply with §106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period: seven years
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department maintains that seven years is the appropriate length of time that records must be maintained under the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may retain records for a longer period if they choose or because of other legal obligations (e.g., concerns about repeat harassers). The Department declined to tie retention to litigation needs or to base retention on a student's enrollment period, favoring a single standard threshold for administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make all training materials available for public inspection upon request (§106.8(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must make all materials used to provide training under §106.8(d) available upon request for inspection by members of the public, regardless of whether the recipient maintains a website. The final rule removed the requirement to post training materials on a website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘All materials’ includes slides with training content and records from professional development programs used to satisfy training obligations; providing only a certificate of completion is insufficient. Recipients may formalize how inspection requests are made (e.g., onsite inspection with a representative present) to protect proprietary information and privacy interests. If third-party materials contain proprietary content and the provider will not permit public inspection, the recipient cannot use those materials to meet §106.8(d)(2) training obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect nondisclosure of personally identifiable information (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(j) prohibits a recipient from disclosing personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with the Title IX regulations except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must comply with §106.44(j) and other Federal, State, and local laws (e.g., FERPA, HIPAA) regarding dissemination of data. Nothing in §106.8 requires records to be disclosed, and recipients must also follow §106.45 and §106.46 requirements regarding provision of evidence and determination of responsibility. §106.45(f)(4)(iii) further requires reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized disclosure by parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require deletion or correction of records when complaints dismissed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to add language requiring a recipient to delete records when a complaint is dismissed or an informal resolution concludes without a finding or admission of responsibility, or to require correction of such records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining records of dismissal or informal resolution outcomes is necessary to demonstrate compliance; if judicial determinations change the recipient's determination, those changes are included in retained records under §106.8(f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: No pregnancy-specific recordkeeping requirement (proposed §106.8(f)(4) removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department removed proposed §106.8(f)(4), which would have required recordkeeping specifically related to pregnancy and related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department determined such a requirement was unnecessary for OCR compliance assessment, presented privacy risks and a chilling effect, and could conflict with FERPA/HIPAA concerns. Documentation relevant to pregnancy-related complaints remains covered by general recordkeeping requirements (§106.8(f)(1)-(2)) and confidentiality protections in §106.44(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor for barriers to reporting and take steps to address them (§106.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must monitor for barriers to reporting sex discrimination in its education program or activity and take steps reasonably calculated to address those barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barriers to reporting impede complainants and the recipient's ability to address sex discrimination; §106.44(b) is necessary to effectuate Title IX and the Department's enforcement authority under 20 U.S.C. 1682.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee notification duties to the Title IX Coordinator (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(c), employees are either required to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, or to provide the contact information of the Title IX Coordinator and information about how to make a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures information reaches the Title IX Coordinator even if a complainant does not know how to contact them; the recordkeeping obligation is tied to such notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize confidential employees and provide disclosure channels (§106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.44(d) recognizes the role of confidential employees who provide services and allows recipients to communicate which employees have confidential status and how to make a complaint to the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should identify confidential resources and explain how disclosures to them are handled (i.e., that such disclosures may not trigger Title IX Coordinator action), consistent with the goal of offering confidential avenues while ensuring Title IX obligations are met when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address disclosures made at public awareness events (§106.44(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.44(e) governs how a recipient responds to information about sex-based harassment disclosed during public awareness events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public awareness events are an important prevention tool; recipients must have procedures for responding to disclosures made in those settings while balancing confidentiality and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibilities to take specific action (§106.44(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.44(f) sets out Title IX Coordinator requirements, including taking specific action in response to information about sexual harassment or sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator actions are integral to a recipient's duty to operate programs free from sex discrimination and to effectuate Title IX; these duties align with other obligations such as offering supportive measures and monitoring barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to offer supportive measures (§106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.44(g) requires recipients to offer supportive measures to complainants and others affected by sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are part of the recipient's response obligations and should be documented as part of the response to notifications; they help remedy effects and prevent further harm while any grievance process proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain evidence-provision and protections against unauthorized party disclosure (§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.45, recipients must comply with obligations regarding the provision of evidence and determination of responsibility, and §106.45(f)(4)(iii) requires taking reasonable steps to prevent and address parties' unauthorized disclosure of information and evidence obtained solely through the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping and evidence-sharing obligations must be balanced with nondisclosure protections; recipients should document evidence provided and steps taken to prevent unauthorized dissemination by parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement safeguards before termination of federal funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Before termination, refusal, or discontinuation of Federal financial assistance, the Department must make an express finding of failure to comply, notify the recipient, attempt voluntary resolution, and provide opportunities for hearing and judicial review (20 U.S.C. 1682-1683; 34 CFR 100.7(d), 100.8(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's enforcement process begins with notice of alleged violations and seeks voluntary corrective action negotiated with the recipient; resolutions are fact-specific and account for the recipient type and investigative findings. These safeguards protect recipients from sudden fund termination and mitigate concerns about strict liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory interpretation consistent with constitutional protections (§106.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department maintained §106.6(d), which states that nothing in the Title IX regulations requires a recipient to restrict rights protected against government action by the U.S. Constitution (e.g., First, Fifth, and Fourteenth Amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of prior ‘deliberate indifference’ language from §106.44 does not alter §106.6(d); recipients should interpret their obligations in a manner consistent with constitutional guarantees, and the Department intends enforcement to be consistent with First Amendment and other constitutional rights.
